Name: Marty Supreme
Review: What a phenomenal movie. A great fucking movie. If I had to describe it in a single sentence I would say it is one hellishly frenzied tale of human obsession and strive for greatness. Mauser's own fate is already so fully realised inside his own mind that it seeps into the whole universe of this movie. Everything else around him, his family, his friends become just pawns for him to actualise his vision of becoming the world's greatest ping-pong player. Adamant and unyielding in all his efforts, nothing can stop this guy. And nothing does. He quenches his thirst of glory and becomes what he was always supposed to be, the greatest. Before he can achieve greatness he involves himself(or is rather forced to) in all of these seemingly absurd and incredibly funny situations that are like a 20th century caricature of the trials of Odysseus, mostly orbiting around him needing money for his tournaments. Great stuff, I absolutely adore the comedic side of this movie. This movie is most definitely a product our times. The world is driven by individualism, self-actualisation, and an all-for-yourself mentality. These themes are all well reflected by the movie, and maybe even more so by the actor. Chalamet is a great pick for this role and, in a metatextual way, he's kind of playing himself. He keeps putting out amazing performances and may even become one of the greatest actors of our time. His acting in this movie leaves nothing to be desired, and that applies for the other actors as well. "That doesn't even enter my consciousness." I need to start getting into this mindset.
